reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes signup-linked trading rewards and presents using a free Bitcoin bonus to enter Terra Luna as having zero-risk exposure. The video also promotes buying or holding Terra Luna around a possible airdrop and a volatility event as potential opportunities. The speaker warns that Terra Luna is volatile, buyers could be left with losses, and snapshot timing could change, so no guaranteed outcome or confirmed loss is established.

a lot of people are gearing up to trade the potential volatility on May 27th

if you guys do want to buy Terra Luna, it is not too late

opening.argument: The presentation is explicit about uncertainty and downside, which weighs against reading it as a promise of easy gains. The speaker says Terra Luna could fall sharply, describes money as capable of being both made and lost, and warns that the proposed snapshot time could change. He also tells viewers to do their own research and describes uninformed buyers getting stuck holding the bag. Those warnings give viewers reasons to question the opportunity rather than treating it as safe or guaranteed.

citations.quote: I imagine that we could see Lunaterra fall off a cliff shortly after
there's a lot of money to be made and lost this week when it comes to Terra Luna
that could change at this point in the game
everybody has to do their own research
they get stuck holding the bag.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited buying and holding language does not stand alone. The speaker presents several possible outcomes, including a drastic fall, says the snapshot timing could change, and warns that uninformed buyers may be left holding losses. The prosecution identifies real promotional language, but its quotes do not establish that the speaker promised either an airdrop or a profitable trade.

citations.quote: scenario one it would go up in value and then drop drastically in value
that could change at this point in the game
they get stuck holding the bag.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk warnings do not erase the actionable purchase guidance. The speaker still tells viewers they can buy Terra Luna, identifies a date on which to hold it for the snapshot, and calls buying the easiest way to seek the airdrop. He also points to a possible price increase. The outcome is uncertain, but the token participation being promoted is clear.

opening.argument: The central discussion is conditional market analysis around the snapshot. The speaker lays out competing paths: a rise followed by a drastic fall, a rise that returns to its starting point, and further buying driven by FOMO. He also explains a practical uncertainty for holders: an exchange may decline to list the new asset. This is an attempt to examine how the event might affect trading and access, not a claim that appreciation is inevitable.

citations.quote: let's go over a couple of different I guess theories that are circling out there so that you can get a better understanding of how to trade terra luna on may 27th
it would go up in value and then drop drastically in value
Terraluna takes off and then comes right back down to where it took off from
all of a sudden, FOMO kicks in
i wouldn't expect every exchange to list the new terra luna

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution quotes possible buying and price movement, but the surrounding discussion asks why holders might sell and what could go wrong after the snapshot. The speaker describes speculative theories, including a reversal, and notes that exchange support is uncertain. Those details support reading the video as analysis of a volatile event rather than a certification that buying will pay off.

citations.quote: there are some holders right now who only want to hold for the airdrop
We've got FOMO buyers jumping
i wouldn't expect every exchange to list the new terra luna
They may limit buying and selling, and so on.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The scenario format does not make the video merely observational. The speaker turns the event analysis into guidance to buy for an airdrop, hold on a specified snapshot date, and consider trading anticipated volatility. The uncertainty around those outcomes limits any promise of success, but it does not remove the purchase and appreciation pitch.

opening.argument: The commercial elements shown are account and exchange promotions, with no demonstrated deposit-to-the-speaker arrangement, credential request, or recruitment scheme. The speaker mentions an account signup offer and a platform where Terra Luna can be bought or sold, but he also states that transfers off that platform are unavailable and cautions that exchanges might not list the new asset. The supplied material therefore supports a narrower reading: ordinary platform promotion alongside risky trading commentary, without evidence of a guaranteed-return arrangement.

citations.quote: got a link in the description for weeble super simple to set up your account
Voyager allows you to buy and sell right now
you cannot transfer it off platform
i wouldn't expect every exchange to list the new terra luna

rebuttal.rebuttal: The signup offer and exchange mention show commercial promotion, but neither quoted passage establishes a hidden fee, guaranteed profit, payment to the speaker, or recruitment requirement. The speaker also discloses a transfer limitation and says exchanges may restrict trading or reject the new project. The prosecution's cited pathway is risky, but the supplied evidence does not establish those additional deceptive mechanisms.

citations.quote: you cannot transfer it off platform
They may limit buying and selling, and so on.
they may scrap the project altogether

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of those other mechanisms does not answer the central concern. The speaker links buying and holding Terra Luna to obtaining a new airdrop, promotes access to trading, and highlights a possible price increase around the snapshot. Disclosure of exchange limitations does not undo that token purchase and appreciation pitch.
